newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan delays decision on 50,000 T sugar import.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan delays decision on 50,000 T sugar import.

text.p: The state-run Trading Corporation of Pakistan said on Monday it had delayed a decision on bids received for the import of 50,000 tonnes of sugar.
A TCP official said the Karachi-based corporation had sent a report on the bidding to Islamabad, where a government committee was expected to discuss the issue on Thursday.
He said the report contained a recommendation that Pakistan buy sugar only from the 1996/97 (July-June) crop and not accept sugar from the 1995/96 crop as offered by one Indian bidder.
The TCP received nine bids to supply 50,000 tonnes of crystal white sugar for shipment by December 31.
The government issued the tender because of a shortfall due to the delayed start of the domestic sugarcane crushing season, which began last month rather than in October as usual.
The TCP and private importers had bought more than 425,000 tonnes of sugar by October. The TCP official did not say if there was any import target for the whole of 1996/97.
